title: Bonus Episode: The Role of Body and Dash Cams in Policing with Nick Camp, PhD

sentences.en: Hey, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: It's Caitlin Luna, host of Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是《心理学谈话》的主持人凯特琳·卢娜。

sentences.en: This episode was recorded during
sentences.zh: 本期节目是在

sentences.en: APA's Technology, Mind, and Society conference held in October 2019 in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 2019年10月于华盛顿特区举办的美国心理学会（APA）“技术、思维与社会”会议期间录制的。

sentences.en: I was away on maternity leave during that time, so my colleague Kim Mills was a guest hoSt. We hope you like this episode.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在休产假，所以由我的同事金·米尔斯担任客座主持。希望大家喜欢这期节目。

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a biweekly podcast from the American Psychological Association that looks at the connections between psychological science
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会推出的一档双周播客，旨在探讨心理科学

sentences.en: and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Kim Mills, and I'm coming to you from APA's annual Technology,
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯，现在正在华盛顿特区参加APA的年度“技术、

sentences.en: Mind, and Society conference in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 思维与社会”会议。

sentences.en: That's a cross-disciplinary meeting that is examining psychology's role in advancing everything from virtual reality to artificial intelligence to the Internet of Things.
sentences.zh: 这是一场跨学科会议，旨在审视心理学在推动从虚拟现实、人工智能到物联网等各个领域发展中的作用。

sentences.en: Cameras are playing a greater and greater role in law enforcement, whether we're talking about cameras placed on dashboards and police cruisers or cameras that
sentences.zh: 摄像头在执法中的作用越来越大，无论是安装在仪表盘和警车上的摄像头，还是

sentences.en: officers wear as part of their uniforMs. But how effective are cameras in police encounters?
sentences.zh: 警员制服上佩戴的摄像头。但这些摄像头在警察执法过程中到底有多有效呢？

sentences.en: What do they tell us about police-citizen interactions?
sentences.zh: 它们能告诉我们关于警民互动的什么信息？

sentences.en: And do cameras ever lie?
sentences.zh: 摄像头会撒谎吗？

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Nick Camp, a postdoctoral researcher at Stanford University, where he received his Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是斯坦福大学的博士后研究员尼克·坎普博士，他在那里获得了博士学位，

sentences.en: after completing his B.A.
sentences.zh: 此前他在哥伦比亚大学

sentences.en: at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 获得了学士学位。

sentences.en: His primary research focus examines racial disparities in the everyday encounters between police officers and citizens.
sentences.zh: 他的主要研究方向是警民日常互动中的种族差异。

sentences.en: To understand the causes and consequences of these inequities, he draws on a range of methods, from computational studies
sentences.zh: 为了理解这些不平等现象的成因和后果，他运用了多种研究方法，从对

sentences.en: of officers' body-worn camera footage, to experiments in community and lab settings, to analyses of traffic stop data.
sentences.zh: 警员随身摄像头拍摄的视频进行计算分析，到社区和实验室环境中的实验，再到对交通拦截数据的分析。

sentences.en: Dr. Camp, thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 坎普博士，感谢您参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So let me start by asking you, how common are cameras in police work today?
sentences.zh: 那么，我想先问一下，如今摄像头在警务工作中有多普遍？

sentences.en: Is every police force in America using them or considering using them?
sentences.zh: 美国的每个警察部门都在使用或考虑使用它们吗？

sentences.en: So a recent survey shows that almost every police department in the country has either deployed these cameras or is planning to in the near future.
sentences.zh: 最近的一项调查显示，全国几乎每个警察部门要么已经部署了这些摄像头，要么计划在不久的将来部署。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is a rare reform that both police agencies and the public have been in favor of.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一项罕见的、警察机构和公众都支持的改革。

sentences.en: So it's been a pretty rapid rollout of this technology.
sentences.zh: 所以这项技术的推广速度非常快。

sentences.en: So how are cameras changing police work?
sentences.zh: 那么摄像头是如何改变警务工作的呢？

sentences.en: And on balance, would you say that change is more for the good?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，您认为这种改变更多是积极的吗？

sentences.en: So there's a few different ways and a few different effects that people have looked at with these cameras.
sentences.zh: 人们对这些摄像头关注的重点和产生的影响有几种不同的看法。

sentences.en: So the first earliest studies have just looked at, does having these cameras make a difference in police community trust?
sentences.zh: 最早的一些研究只是关注：拥有这些摄像头是否会改变警民之间的信任？

sentences.en: And the results are mixed, but on the whole, simply having police officers recording these encounters gives citizens a sense of security that
sentences.zh: 结果不尽相同，但总的来说，仅仅让警员记录这些互动，就能给公民一种安全感，即

sentences.en: police officers will be held accountable for their actions.
sentences.zh: 警员会为自己的行为负责。

sentences.en: So other research has looked at what we can actually, you know, see on these videos and there, the data is also kind of mixed.
sentences.zh: 其他研究则关注我们实际上能在这些视频中看到什么，这方面的数据也比较混杂。

sentences.en: In many cases, the footage can be kind of ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，视频内容可能有些模糊不清。

sentences.en: So it's hard to tell, but my research looks at the language and what these cameras capture about everyday interactions.
sentences.zh: 所以很难判断，但我的研究关注的是语言，以及这些摄像头捕捉到的日常互动信息。

sentences.en: And I think this is really a new source of data for departments and can really be used to measure police reform for good.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是警察部门的一项新数据来源，可以真正用于衡量警务改革的成效。

sentences.en: So how can the footage be ambiguous?
sentences.zh: 那么视频内容怎么会模糊不清呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, a camera is a camera.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，摄像头就是摄像头。

sentences.en: It takes a picture of what's happening, right?
sentences.zh: 它拍下了正在发生的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, how could it be open to interpretation?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它怎么会有解读空间呢？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, the hope was, you know, the camera doesn't lie and simply putting a camera
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们原本希望摄像头不会撒谎，给每位警员

sentences.en: on every police officer would give us an unbiased view of what's actually happening in these encounters.
sentences.zh: 佩戴摄像头能让我们客观地看到这些互动中到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, the camera is positioned on the police officer about chest level.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，摄像头是安装在警员胸部位置的。

sentences.en: So if you imagine filming a movie with a camera at that level, you don't see a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想象一下用那个高度的摄像机拍电影，你是看不到太多东西的。

sentences.en: And the fact that it's filmed from the police officer's perspective, research by Broderick Turner and others has shown that this kind of leads people to empathize with the officer.
sentences.zh: 而且由于它是从警员的角度拍摄的，布罗德里克·特纳等人的研究表明，这会导致人们对警员产生共情。

sentences.en: So you're really getting literally one point of view in these interactions.
sentences.zh: 所以你在这些互动中实际上只得到了一个视角。

sentences.en: Has there been thought given to changing where the camera is worn, like soldiers wear cameras on their helmets now?
sentences.zh: 有没有考虑过改变摄像头的佩戴位置，比如士兵现在把摄像头戴在头盔上？

sentences.en: So there are a few, the technology is advancing quite rapidly.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些，技术正在迅速进步。

sentences.en: So some police departments are trying to position cameras in other locations in the uniform.
sentences.zh: 所以一些警察部门正在尝试将摄像头安装在制服的其他位置。

sentences.en: But the fact of the matter is at the end of the day, it's going to be on the police officer.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，归根结底，它还是会戴在警员身上。

sentences.en: And so some of these are just limitations of the footage.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些只是视频本身的局限性。

sentences.en: So your research has used body camera footage to look at racial disparities and how police officers communicate with citizens.
sentences.zh: 您的研究利用随身摄像头视频来观察种族差异以及警员与公民的沟通方式。

sentences.en: What have you found?
sentences.zh: 您发现了什么？

sentences.en: So this was a project that started, originally, we were planning to look at the video from these interactions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个项目，最初我们计划观察这些互动视频。

sentences.en: And again, since the camera's at chest level, we didn't really see a whole lot of the community members that police officers were talking to.
sentences.zh: 同样，由于摄像头在胸部位置，我们并没有真正看到太多警员正在交谈的社区成员。

sentences.en: But I noticed as I was watching this footage that the words were coming in loud and clear.
sentences.zh: 但我注意到，在观看这些视频时，谈话内容听得非常清楚。

sentences.en: And so what we did was we looked at the words that officers were using in their conversations with black and white drivers that they stopped.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的是分析警员在拦截黑人和白人司机时所使用的言辞。

sentences.en: And we found using a range of different methods that police officers communicate more respectfully when they're talking
sentences.zh: 我们利用多种不同的方法发现，警员在与白人司机交谈时

sentences.en: to white drivers than when they're talking to African Americans.
sentences.zh: 比与非裔美国人交谈时表现得更尊重。

sentences.en: Do you know, has your research indicated who's more heavily influenced by the body cameras, whether it's the police or the civilians?
sentences.zh: 您知道您的研究是否表明谁受随身摄像头的影响更大吗，是警察还是平民？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: One of our current projects is asking police officers and community members to look at the same interaction and see how their judgments about how respectful the officers being
sentences.zh: 我们目前的一个项目是要求警员和社区成员观看同一段互动，看看他们对警员表现得有多尊重

sentences.en: or how combative the drivers being, how that might differ across perspectives.
sentences.zh: 或者司机表现得有多好斗的判断，在不同视角下会有什么不同。

sentences.en: So that's a really great point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的切入点。

sentences.en: And it's something that we're looking into.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们正在研究的内容。

sentences.en: So we don't know yet whether civilians are also more respectful.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还不知道平民是否也会表现得更尊重。

sentences.en: I mean, do they always know that the cop is wearing a camera?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们总是知道警察戴着摄像头吗？

sentences.en: So that differs from agency to agency.
sentences.zh: 这因机构而异。

sentences.en: Some agencies make a point of having officers mention that they have a camera in the recording.
sentences.zh: 一些机构要求警员在录音中明确提到他们佩戴了摄像头。

sentences.en: Other agencies, the policy is just for the officer to turn on the camera before they make contact with the driver.
sentences.zh: 其他机构的政策只是要求警员在与司机接触前打开摄像头。

sentences.en: So these are all great questions.
sentences.zh: 这些都是很好的问题。

sentences.en: And I think it's an empirical question as to whether announcing the camera puts citizens at ease more than simply having it on.
sentences.zh: 我认为，宣布有摄像头是否比仅仅佩戴它更能让公民感到安心，这是一个实证问题。

sentences.en: What about individuals' right to privacy?
sentences.zh: 那么个人的隐私权呢？

sentences.en: I mean, do you have any right to privacy if a police officer is stopping you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果警察拦下你，你还有隐私权吗？

sentences.en: Can you say, I want you to turn that camera off?
sentences.zh: 你可以说，我要求你关掉那个摄像头吗？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And I think as these cameras and the footage they capture are being deployed, I think we're going to have more of these kinds of questions as to who can access the
sentences.zh: 我认为随着这些摄像头及其捕捉到的视频被广泛使用，我们将会有更多关于谁可以访问这些

sentences.en: footage and what circumstances.
sentences.zh: 视频以及在什么情况下访问的问题。

sentences.en: As of right now, it's lawful for police officers to make these recordings.
sentences.zh: 目前，警员进行这些录制是合法的。

sentences.en: And to my knowledge, I don't think you can ask that that encounter not be recorded.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，你不能要求不录制那次互动。

sentences.en: But for example, there's ongoing debates about whether police officers should have access to that body camera footage.
sentences.zh: 但例如，关于警员是否应该有权查看这些随身摄像头视频，目前仍存在争议。

sentences.en: If so, can they view it before or after they give a statement about an incident?
sentences.zh: 如果可以，他们能在就事件发表声明之前或之后查看吗？

sentences.en: Can the public view this?
sentences.zh: 公众可以查看吗？

sentences.en: And really, this is a frontier and this is a place where psychologists can help inform these policies.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个前沿领域，也是心理学家可以帮助提供政策建议的地方。

sentences.en: So there's no standard procedure at this point for how and where these videos are stored.
sentences.zh: 所以目前对于这些视频如何存储以及存储在哪里，还没有统一的程序。

sentences.en: You're saying that we just don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 您的意思是说我们还不知道。

sentences.en: It's still being shaken out.
sentences.zh: 一切还在摸索中。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's differences in agencies as to how long videos are stored for, because as you
sentences.zh: 各机构在视频存储时长上存在差异，因为正如你

sentences.en: imagine, it's very easy for police departments to accumulate tons and tons of videos, what purposes they're being used for.
sentences.zh: 想象的那样，警察部门很容易积累海量的视频，而且这些视频的用途也各不相同。

sentences.en: So this is really a rapidly developing field.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一个快速发展的领域。

sentences.en: So what do we learn from, say, dash cameras that are different from what we might learn from a body camera?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们从行车记录仪中学到的东西，与从随身摄像头中学到的有什么不同？

sentences.en: So dash cameras are interesting because you can see both actors on them.
sentences.zh: 行车记录仪很有趣，因为你可以看到双方当事人。

sentences.en: There's some new technologies that pair dash cameras with microphones or with body cameras.
sentences.zh: 有一些新技术将行车记录仪与麦克风或随身摄像头配对。

sentences.en: You can get different views on the same event.
sentences.zh: 你可以从同一事件中获得不同的视角。

sentences.en: One piece of research that's been really interesting, Yale Grinot and colleagues have
sentences.zh: 有一项研究非常有趣，耶鲁大学的格里诺特及其同事

sentences.en: used eye tracking to look at how people, when they view dashboard camera videos, where they're actually looking in the scene.
sentences.zh: 利用眼动追踪技术观察人们在观看行车记录仪视频时，实际上在关注场景中的什么位置。

sentences.en: And again, people's pre-existing beliefs and trust in the police can guide where they're actually watching in these interactions.
sentences.zh: 同样，人们预先存在的信念和对警察的信任会引导他们在这些互动中关注不同的地方。

sentences.en: So again, it's another great opportunity and another rich source of data.
sentences.zh: 所以这又是另一个很好的机会，也是一个丰富的数据来源。

sentences.en: But it's also something that we have to remember that individual minds are going to be viewing and interpreting.
sentences.zh: 但我们也必须记住，这是由个人的思维在观看和解读。

sentences.en: So what's happening with body cameras and training in police forces right now?
sentences.zh: 那么目前警察部队中随身摄像头和培训的情况如何？

sentences.en: I mean, is that something that is discussed?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个讨论的话题吗？

sentences.en: And when you're in the police academy, you're learning how to use a body cam and when to turn that on, when to turn on a dash cam?
sentences.zh: 当你在警察学院时，你会学习如何使用随身摄像头，以及何时打开它，何时打开行车记录仪吗？

sentences.en: What's the training like right now?
sentences.zh: 现在的培训是什么样的？

sentences.en: So first of all, police officers love body cameras.
sentences.zh: 首先，警员们很喜欢随身摄像头。

sentences.en: They have the belief that having these interactions recorded in case they get a complaint will protect them.
sentences.zh: 他们认为记录下这些互动可以保护他们，以防遭到投诉。

sentences.en: So it's in police officers' interest to properly use these cameras and record their interactions.
sentences.zh: 所以正确使用这些摄像头并记录互动符合警员的利益。

sentences.en: One thing that is kind of on the cutting edge is using these recordings for training purposes.
sentences.zh: 目前处于前沿的一点是利用这些录像进行培训。

sentences.en: And this is something that my team and I are very interested in, not just for looking at specific acute instances, such as use
sentences.zh: 这也是我和我的团队非常感兴趣的事情，不仅仅是观察特定的突发事件，例如使用

sentences.en: of force cases, but looking at like police officers' communication.
sentences.zh: 武力案件，而是观察警员的沟通方式。

sentences.en: So one of the greatest tools that a police officer has is their words.
sentences.zh: 警员拥有的最伟大的工具之一就是他们的语言。

sentences.en: And if we can better train police officers in how to communicate with the public, it can prevent many of these interactions from escalating to the use of force.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能更好地培训警员如何与公众沟通，就能防止许多互动升级为武力冲突。

sentences.en: And it is pretty much acceptable among police officers.
sentences.zh: 而且这在警员中基本上是可以接受的。

sentences.en: You said that they really like them and you said that the public likes these cameras as well, but I know there's been a lot of controversy in certain cases.
sentences.zh: 你说他们真的很喜欢，而且你说公众也喜欢这些摄像头，但我知道在某些情况下存在很多争议。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of cases that make it into the media and it turns out that there's some dispute over what really happened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多进入媒体视野的案件，结果对到底发生了什么存在争议。

sentences.en: And you talked about, you know, the difference in angles.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了角度的差异。

sentences.en: So is it really all that popular basically?
sentences.zh: 所以它真的那么受欢迎吗？

sentences.en: So the challenge is that many times when we're talking about body camera footage, it's in the context of particular incidents, trying to decide who's in the right,
sentences.zh: 挑战在于，很多时候当我们谈论随身摄像头视频时，都是在特定事件的背景下，试图决定谁是对的，

sentences.en: who is in the wrong, and specifically in very ambiguous incidents.
sentences.zh: 谁是错的，特别是在非常模糊的事件中。

sentences.en: And unfortunately that ambiguous, those ambiguous circumstances are the cases where people's individual biases might shape how they interpret that footage.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，那些模糊的情况正是人们的个人偏见可能影响他们如何解读视频的案例。

sentences.en: It's already can be a pretty fuzzy signal.
sentences.zh: 这本身可能就是一个非常模糊的信号。

sentences.en: So I think that's one reason why we see a lot of debate over the meaning of particular videos and what they capture and what they don't capture.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是为什么我们看到对特定视频的含义、它们捕捉到了什么以及没捕捉到什么存在大量争论的原因之一。

sentences.en: But at the same time, one of the things I hope to show in my research is there are thousands of interactions between police officers and the public, and many of them are not
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我希望在我的研究中展示的一点是，警员与公众之间有成千上万次互动，其中许多并不

sentences.en: ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 模糊。

sentences.en: And particularly the words that officers use, many are evidently respectful or disrespectful.
sentences.zh: 特别是警员使用的言辞，许多明显是尊重或不尊重的。

sentences.en: So what I'm hoping is that in addition to using these videos as evidence in particular cases, we can use it as a source of data to look at policing as a whole.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望，除了将这些视频作为特定案件的证据外，我们还能将其作为数据来源，从整体上审视警务工作。

sentences.en: Are you doing, or is anybody doing research into the change in language that may be occurring as a result of using cameras?
sentences.zh: 您是否正在，或者有人正在研究因使用摄像头而可能发生的语言变化吗？

sentences.en: So yeah, that's a very tricky question because, you know, it always comes down to like, what's the baseline?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常棘手的问题，因为你知道，它总是归结为：基准是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, what can you compare it to, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，你拿什么来比较，对吧？

sentences.en: Not to mention that these cameras are proliferating so rapidly, it's hard to get a control group.
sentences.zh: 更不用说这些摄像头普及得如此之快，很难找到对照组。

sentences.en: Um, so that is a challenging question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这是一个具有挑战性的问题。

sentences.en: And I don't know if we're past the point where we're going to be able to answer what's the effect of having body cameras, versus what can we learn from the footage
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们是否已经过了能够回答“拥有随身摄像头的影响是什么”这一问题的阶段，相比之下，我们能从它们捕捉到的

sentences.en: that they're capturing?
sentences.zh: 视频中学到什么？

sentences.en: So what else are you looking at now?
sentences.zh: 那么您现在还在研究什么？

sentences.en: Where's your research headed?
sentences.zh: 您的研究方向是什么？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: So there's a few different directions.
sentences.zh: 有几个不同的方向。

sentences.en: Um, one very basic psychological question is, in addition to, you know, what's the information captured in these recordings?
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个非常基础的心理学问题是，除了这些录音中捕捉到的信息外，

sentences.en: What can these recordings tell us about how people form or lose their trust in the police?
sentences.zh: 这些录音能告诉我们人们是如何建立或失去对警察的信任的？

sentences.en: So in some research, we've been looking at police officers tone of voice.
sentences.zh: 在一些研究中，我们一直在观察警员的说话语气。

sentences.en: So we filter out the words from these recordings.
sentences.zh: 我们过滤掉了录音中的词汇。

sentences.en: And so you're left with something like a Charlie Brown, grown up type of language, like, and we're interested in how one, this tone might differ when police officers are
sentences.zh: 所以你剩下的是类似《查理·布朗》中成年人那种声音，我们感兴趣的是，当警员

sentences.en: talking to white and black men to have people's pre existing trust in the police shapes what they hear in that, um, Charlie Brown signal.
sentences.zh: 与白人和黑人男性交谈时，这种语气有何不同，以及人们预先存在的对警察的信任如何塑造了他们在那种“查理·布朗”信号中听到的内容。

sentences.en: And then third, if you only expose people to police officers interactions with white drivers or black drivers, how would that shape their perception of the police department?
sentences.zh: 第三，如果你只让人们接触警员与白人司机或黑人司机的互动，这会如何塑造他们对警察部门的看法？

sentences.en: And what we're finding is first police officers use a more respectful tone when they're talking to white men.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，首先，警员在与白人男性交谈时使用的语气更尊重。

sentences.en: Second, that people's own individual trust in the police shapes how trustworthy they perceive that tone.
sentences.zh: 其次，人们自己对警察的个人信任塑造了他们认为那种语气有多值得信赖。

sentences.en: And then third, that people who are exposed to police officer interactions with black men think that the police department is less trustworthy than those who
sentences.zh: 第三，那些接触过警员与黑人男性互动的人，认为警察部门比那些

sentences.en: listen to many interactions with white men.
sentences.zh: 听过许多与白人男性互动的人更不值得信任。

sentences.en: So that's kind of one additional way we can use this to expose different people to the same exact interaction.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是我们利用这种方法让不同的人接触到完全相同的互动方式的另一种途径。

sentences.en: Uh, in other research we're looking at what's the relationship between, uh, these acute instances of police violence and how those might
sentences.zh: 嗯，在其他研究中，我们正在探讨这些突发的警察暴力事件与它们如何

sentences.en: color the everyday interactions between police officers and communities of color.
sentences.zh: 影响警察与有色人种社区之间的日常互动，这两者之间存在怎样的联系。

sentences.en: So for me, what's really exciting is that having access to, to body camera footage really opens up a whole new world of questions.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，真正令人兴奋的是，能够获取随身摄像头的录像，确实开启了一个全新的问题领域。

sentences.en: And I think it'll really help us understand how this relationship can be built and how trust can be formed or eroded in these interactions.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的能帮助我们理解这种关系是如何建立的，以及在这些互动中信任是如何形成或被侵蚀的。

sentences.en: Are you looking at differences with other demographic groups, for example, women or Latinos or people of ambiguous racial or ethnic backgrounds?
sentences.zh: 你们是否在研究与其他人口统计学群体之间的差异，例如女性、拉丁裔，或者种族或族裔背景模糊的人群？

sentences.en: So absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: Um, in our initial study, we looked at just black and white drivers, single month.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们最初的研究中，我们只观察了黑人和白人司机，为期一个月。

sentences.en: Uh, we did look at gender police officers generally use more respectful language with female drivers,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实研究了性别，警察通常对女性司机使用更尊重的语言，

sentences.en: but in, uh, our next wave of research, really opening it up to look at, um, a wider range of interactions.
sentences.zh: 但在我们下一阶段的研究中，我们确实会扩大范围，去观察更广泛的互动。

sentences.en: One of the challenges from our approach, since we focus so much on language is when police officers are conversing with people who, um, English is not their native language.
sentences.zh: 我们方法面临的挑战之一，因为我们非常关注语言，就是当警察与那些英语并非母语的人交谈时。

sentences.en: That's a challenge we have to deal with.
sentences.zh: 这是我们必须应对的一个挑战。

sentences.en: Um, especially since many police officers in the department we study, uh, can speak Spanish.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是因为我们研究的部门中许多警察都会说西班牙语。

sentences.en: Um, but I think these are challenges that, you know, will advance our understanding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为这些挑战，你知道，会推动我们进一步理解。

sentences.en: So initially we focused on one specific contrast, but hopefully we can learn more about policing across a range of identities.
sentences.zh: 所以最初我们专注于一个特定的对比，但希望我们能更多地了解跨越不同身份的警务工作。

sentences.en: What got you interested in this aspect of psychology?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你对心理学的这个方面产生了兴趣？

sentences.en: So my path has been kind of a, a backwards one.
sentences.zh: 我的路径可以说是一种倒退的路径。

sentences.en: Um, um, I didn't really think that much about race until I became a psychologiSt. And for me,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在成为心理学家之前，我并没有太考虑种族问题。对我来说，

sentences.en: one of the powerful messages of psychology is it can show you different ways of seeing and thinking about the world.
sentences.zh: 心理学的一个有力信息是，它可以向你展示看待和思考世界的不同方式。

sentences.en: And for someone who, before he took a psychology course, believe that people could just put their identities at the door and, you know, be a good student or be a good worker.
sentences.zh: 对于一个在修读心理学课程之前，还相信人们可以把自己的身份抛在门外，成为一名好学生或好员工的人来说，

sentences.en: It really took a, the research on stereotype threat and a lot of social psychology to just show to me that that wasn't the case.
sentences.zh: 确实需要关于刻板印象威胁的研究和大量的社会心理学知识，才能向我证明事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And I think once I was disabused of that idea, I really became hungry for, to learn more.
sentences.zh: 我想一旦我摆脱了那种想法，我就真的渴望学习更多。

sentences.en: So as, in terms of when I became interested in policing specifically,
sentences.zh: 至于我具体是什么时候对警务工作产生兴趣的，

sentences.en: a lot of my early work in grad school was looking at, uh, face perception.
sentences.zh: 我在研究生院早期的大部分工作都是在研究面部感知。

sentences.en: And so I was spending hours and hours a day, morphing faces, running these lab studies with faces and Michael Brown was, uh, was shot.
sentences.zh: 所以我每天花上几个小时进行面部变形，在实验室里用人脸做研究，当时迈克尔·布朗被枪杀了。

sentences.en: And I thought, okay, like, why am I doing this research?
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我为什么要进行这项研究？

sentences.en: I think perception's incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 我认为感知非常重要。

sentences.en: And I think that can tell us a lot, but at the end of the day, what I really found interesting about that work was that it could speak to broader issues of, of racial inequality.
sentences.zh: 我认为这能告诉我们很多，但归根结底，我发现这项工作真正有趣的地方在于，它能触及种族不平等的更广泛议题。

sentences.en: And so I think that really pushed me to focus on not just these very basic research projects, but looking at how race, uh, and racial inequality plays out in the real world.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这确实促使我不仅关注这些非常基础的研究项目，还要观察种族和种族不平等在现实世界中是如何体现的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: This is real, very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'd like to keep tabs on what you're doing because I think it's important work and it's going to help reduce the inequities that we experience in our country.
sentences.zh: 我想持续关注你的工作，因为我认为这是一项重要的工作，它将有助于减少我们在国内所经历的不平等现象。

sentences.en: Really appreciate you joining us today, Dr. Camp.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天能参加我们的节目，坎普博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: So before we go, let me remind listeners that we want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 在结束之前，让我提醒听众，我们很想听到你们的声音。

sentences.en: You can email your comments and ideas to speakingofpsychologyatapa.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过电子邮件将你的评论和想法发送至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: And please consider rating us in iTunes.
sentences.zh: 也请考虑在 iTunes 上为我们评分。

sentences.en: We'd appreciate that as well.
sentences.zh: 我们对此也将不胜感激。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is part of the APA podcast network, which includes other informative podcasts, such as APA journals, dialogue about new psychological research and progress
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》是美国心理学会播客网络的一部分，该网络还包括其他信息丰富的播客，例如《APA 期刊》，探讨新的心理学研究和进展，

sentences.en: notes about the practice of psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及关于心理学实践的《笔记》。

sentences.en: You can find all our podcasts on Apple, Stitcher, Spotify, wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Apple、Stitcher、Spotify 或任何你获取播客的地方找到我们所有的节目。

sentences.en: And you can also go to our website, www.speakingofpsychology.org and listen to more episodes.
sentences.zh: 你也可以访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 收听更多剧集。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills with the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学会的基姆·米尔斯。
